inventory.name: Optic canal right
inventory.description: v0.9.137: Common optic canal with an inferolateral ophthalmic-artery recess, separated from the superior orbital fissure by retained optic strut. The optic nerve is not segmented.

inventory.name: Optic canal left
inventory.description: v0.9.137: Common optic canal with an inferolateral ophthalmic-artery recess, separated from the superior orbital fissure by retained optic strut. The optic nerve is not segmented.

inventory.name: Superior orbital fissure right
inventory.description: v0.9.137: Native elongated superior orbital fissure retained; obstructing margins fitted to the medial orbital arteries and preserved ophthalmic venous route. Remains separate from OC and rotundum.

inventory.name: Superior orbital fissure left
inventory.description: v0.9.137: Native elongated superior orbital fissure retained; obstructing margins fitted to the medial orbital arteries and preserved ophthalmic venous route. Remains separate from OC and rotundum.

inventory.name: Inferior orbital fissure right
inventory.description: The inferior orbital fissure is the gap between the orbital floor and lateral wall, communicating with the pterygopalatine and infratemporal regions. It transmits infraorbital and zygomatic neurovascular structures and orbital venous communications.

inventory.name: Inferior orbital fissure left
inventory.description: The inferior orbital fissure is the gap between the orbital floor and lateral wall, communicating with the pterygopalatine and infratemporal regions. It transmits infraorbital and zygomatic neurovascular structures and orbital venous communications.

inventory.name: Infraorbital groove and canal right
inventory.description: The infraorbital groove runs forward on the orbital floor and continues as the infraorbital canal within the maxilla. It carries the infraorbital nerve, artery and vein to the infraorbital foramen.

inventory.name: Infraorbital groove and canal left
inventory.description: The infraorbital groove runs forward on the orbital floor and continues as the infraorbital canal within the maxilla. It carries the infraorbital nerve, artery and vein to the infraorbital foramen.

inventory.name: Infraorbital foramen right
inventory.description: The infraorbital foramen opens on the anterior maxilla below the orbital margin. It transmits the infraorbital nerve, artery and vein to the face.

inventory.name: Infraorbital foramen left
inventory.description: The infraorbital foramen opens on the anterior maxilla below the orbital margin. It transmits the infraorbital nerve, artery and vein to the face.

inventory.name: Anterior ethmoidal canal right
inventory.description: v0.9.137: Anterior ethmoidal foramen and oblique anteromedial canal/groove through the frontoethmoidal roof, then a cranial/falcine exit. Local bone coverage is modelled, not a population statement about dehiscence.

inventory.name: Anterior ethmoidal canal left

inventory.name: Posterior ethmoidal canal right

inventory.name: Posterior ethmoidal canal left
inventory.description: v0.9.137: Separate posterior ethmoidal passage through the posterior frontoethmoidal roof; not conflated with the optic canal or anterior ethmoidal route.

inventory.name: Supraorbital notch or foramen right

inventory.name: Supraorbital notch or foramen left

inventory.name: Cranio-orbital / meningolacrimal canal right
inventory.description: A variable cranio-orbital or meningolacrimal canal in the sphenoid region connects the middle cranial fossa with the orbit. It may transmit a meningolacrimal artery; its presence and relationship to other orbital openings vary.

inventory.name: Cranio-orbital / meningolacrimal canal left

inventory.name: Accessory optic canal left
inventory.description: Variable structure. Presence has not been established; no default route is imposed. v0.9.137: fine olfactory perforations/optional variants remain for batch 7; no obligatory accessory optic or meningolacrimal channel is introduced.

inventory.name: Nasolacrimal canal right
inventory.description: Lacrimal fossa and bony duct corridor to the inferior nasal meatus. The soft lacrimal drainage apparatus is not segmented.

inventory.name: Nasolacrimal canal left
inventory.description: Lacrimal fossa and bony duct corridor to the inferior nasal meatus. The soft lacrimal drainage apparatus is not segmented.

inventory.name: Cribriform foramina right
inventory.description: Selected olfactory perforation group in the cribriform plate, with 10 short channels opening into a continuous subplate olfactory cleft. The crista galli and lateral lamellae are retained. Count and dimensions are illustrative; olfactory nerve filaments are not segmented.

inventory.name: Cribriform foramina left

inventory.description: No reliable coordinate assigned in this mesh review.

inventory.name: Foramen rotundum right
inventory.description: The foramen rotundum is a sphenoid canal connecting the middle cranial fossa with the pterygopalatine fossa. It transmits the maxillary nerve (V2) and small accompanying vessels.

inventory.name: Foramen rotundum left
inventory.description: The foramen rotundum is a sphenoid canal connecting the middle cranial fossa with the pterygopalatine fossa. It transmits the maxillary nerve (V2) and small accompanying vessels.

inventory.name: Foramen ovale right
inventory.description: The foramen ovale opens between the middle cranial fossa and infratemporal region in the greater sphenoid wing. It transmits the mandibular nerve (V3), emissary venous channels and variable small vessels including an accessory meningeal contribution.

inventory.name: Foramen ovale left
inventory.description: The foramen ovale opens between the middle cranial fossa and infratemporal region in the greater sphenoid wing. It transmits the mandibular nerve (V3), emissary venous channels and variable small vessels including an accessory meningeal contribution.

inventory.name: Foramen spinosum right
inventory.description: The foramen spinosum is an opening in the greater sphenoid wing, posterolateral to the foramen ovale. It usually transmits the middle meningeal artery, accompanying veins and the recurrent meningeal branch of V3.

inventory.name: Foramen spinosum left
inventory.description: The foramen spinosum is an opening in the greater sphenoid wing, posterolateral to the foramen ovale. It usually transmits the middle meningeal artery, accompanying veins and the recurrent meningeal branch of V3.

inventory.name: Foramen lacerum right
inventory.description: The foramen lacerum lies at the junction of the sphenoid, petrous temporal and basilar occipital regions and is largely filled by cartilage in life. The internal carotid artery passes over its superior aspect rather than through an open vertical lumen. Petrosal neural and small vascular connections relate to this region.

inventory.name: Foramen lacerum left
inventory.description: The foramen lacerum lies at the junction of the sphenoid, petrous temporal and basilar occipital regions and is largely filled by cartilage in life. The internal carotid artery passes over its superior aspect rather than through an open vertical lumen. Petrosal neural and small vascular connections relate to this region.

inventory.name: Sphenoidal emissary foramen (Vesalius) right
inventory.description: The sphenoidal emissary foramen of Vesalius is a variable opening near the foramen ovale. It commonly carries an emissary venous connection between the cavernous region and pterygoid plexus; small arterial contributions are variable.

inventory.name: Sphenoidal emissary foramen (Vesalius) left
inventory.description: The sphenoidal emissary foramen of Vesalius is a variable opening near the foramen ovale. It commonly carries an emissary venous connection between the cavernous region and pterygoid plexus; small arterial contributions are variable.

inventory.name: Carotid canal left

inventory.name: Facial canal right
inventory.description: v0.9.136: Reference-guided labyrinthine, geniculate, tympanic, second genu and mastoid sequence. Separate from the external acoustic meatus. Segment dimensions and calibre are illustrative.

inventory.name: Facial canal left

inventory.name: Stylomastoid foramen right
inventory.description: The stylomastoid foramen opens between the styloid and mastoid processes and marks the extracranial exit of the facial nerve. The stylomastoid artery accompanies the nerve into the facial canal.

inventory.name: Stylomastoid foramen left
inventory.description: The stylomastoid foramen opens between the styloid and mastoid processes and marks the extracranial exit of the facial nerve. The stylomastoid artery accompanies the nerve into the facial canal.

inventory.name: Petrotympanic fissure right
inventory.description: The petrotympanic fissure communicates between the tympanic region and the mandibular fossa region. Structures associated with it include the chorda tympani and anterior tympanic vessels.

inventory.name: Petrotympanic fissure left
inventory.description: The petrotympanic fissure communicates between the tympanic region and the mandibular fossa region. Structures associated with it include the chorda tympani and anterior tympanic vessels.

inventory.name: Tympanic canaliculus right
inventory.description: The tympanic canaliculus opens near the jugular fossa and carotid canal and ascends to the middle ear. It carries the tympanic branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve and the inferior tympanic artery.

inventory.name: Tympanic canaliculus left

inventory.name: Foramen magnum
inventory.description: The foramen magnum is the large occipital opening between the posterior cranial fossa and vertebral canal. It transmits the medulla-spinal cord transition, meninges, vertebral and spinal vessels and ascending spinal accessory roots. Vertebral dural entry is distinct from passage through the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane.

inventory.description: Anteromedial end of the petrous temporal bone, beside the lacerum region. Marker is on the reviewed bone surface; it is a regional anatomical anchor, not a segmented structure boundary.

inventory.name: Jugular fossa left

inventory.name: Styloid process base left

inventory.name: Sphenoid lingula region left

inventory.name: Petrolingual boundary (estimated) left
inventory.description: The petrolingual ligament forms a regional boundary between the petrous and cavernous ICA in the NYU classification. It extends near the petrous apex and sphenoid lingula; its position is estimated in this atlas.

inventory.name: Carotid sulcus of sphenoid left

inventory.name: Posterior clinoid process left
inventory.description: Lateral end of the dorsum sellae, medial to the posterior cavernous ICA. Marker is on the reviewed bone surface; it is a regional anatomical anchor, not a segmented structure boundary.

inventory.name: Anterior clinoid process left
inventory.description: The anterior clinoid process is the medial projection of the lesser sphenoid wing beside the optic canal and clinoid ICA. It relates to the optic strut, proximal and distal dural rings and the carotid-oculomotor region.

inventory.name: Optic strut region left
inventory.description: v0.9.137: optic-strut marker refitted to retained sphenoid bone between the common optic canal and superior orbital fissure. Positive bone controls verified on each side.

inventory.name: Proximal and distal dural ring region left
inventory.description: The proximal and distal dural rings bound the short clinoid ICA region. The distal ring marks the usual transition to the intradural ICA, with a variable carotid cave medially. This atlas marks a regional estimate rather than separately segmented dural rings.

inventory.name: Sellar floor

inventory.name: Dorsum sellae
inventory.description: Posterior boundary of the hypophyseal fossa, between the posterior clinoids. Marker is on the reviewed bone surface; it is a regional anatomical anchor, not a segmented structure boundary.

inventory.name: Upper clivus
inventory.description: Midline sloping skull-base surface posterior to the sella; the posterior cavernous carotids lie laterally. Marker is on the reviewed bone surface; it is a regional anatomical anchor, not a segmented structure boundary.
